articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday's X-Men Team Officially Confirmed, And It's Not a Line-up Anyone Could Predict
articles.summary: With less than one month until Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters, Marvel has just put out its final trailer for the film and it gives us a more in-depth look at things than ever before. This new trailer shows us more of Steve Rogers' inclusion and what his emotional journey will be, and it cements the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google With less than one month until Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters, Marvel has just put out its final trailer for the film and it gives us a more in-depth look at things than ever before. This new trailer shows us more of Steve Rogers' inclusion and what his emotional journey will be, and it cements the inclusion of some previously unconfirmed characters like Kate Bishop and Cassie Lang, hinting at the Young Avengers . However, the trailer also showcases the X-Men lineup when they actually team up with the other MCU heroes and it isn't a group that anyone likely predicted beforehand.

Going into this film, the casting news revealed who was returning from the original Fox X-Men projects. Professor X, Magneto, Cyclops, Mystique, Beast, and Nightcrawler were confirmed, while Channing Tatum's Gambit from Deadpool & Wolverine is also joining the fray. There have been theories that the X-Men are just there for their universe to be killed off, yet this trailer proves they'll go beyond that and team with the likes of Thor and the Fantastic Four. However, it doesn't seem like everyone will be part of that fight, with some notable omissions teasing a game-changing roster for the X-Men in Avengers: Doomsday .

In the new trailer, we don't even see a member of the X-Men until just before the two-minute mark when Cyclops is shown fighting with Sam Wilson. Their next appearance is the big one, as Cyclops says, "To me, my X-Men, " and members of the team fly in beside him, seemingly for a battle against Doctor Doom and whatever disciples he has with him. From there, Gambit, Mystique, Nightcrawler, and Beast join him, brought in by Nightcrawler's powers. They stand alongside Thor, Sam, Steve, Mr. Fantastic, Yelena, and Shang-Chi.

The two X-Men characters missing are Professor X and Magneto, which hints that maybe they're the people who get killed off. Doom attacking the X-Men's universe and having to get revenge for something devastating happening to the leaders is fitting. It would also make sense to keep them out of the action given the age of Patrick Stewart and Ian McKellen during filming. It also fits the narrative that the X-Men die, yet does it without taking out the entire team.

Of course, there's always a chance that Charles and Erik are off fighting somewhere else. That shot is missing significant heroes like the other members of the Fantastic Four, everyone from Wakanda, and most members of the new group of Avengers. There's also the possibility that this is all a red herring. There's a memorable shot from the Avengers: Infinity War trailer that showed Hulk running in Wakanda with other Avengers, which never happened in the film. That could be what the big team shot here is, though it's unclear.

If this is the official X-Men team, it's one that nobody could've predicted if you told them the characters were returning from Fox. No Wolverine, characters like Jean Grey and Storm missing, and Gambit, who was never with them on the big screen, is there. However, if there really is no Professor X and Magneto as part of the team and they're killed off early, that would really change the dynamic, while also allowing Cyclops to truly feel like the leader.

Do you think Professor X and Magneto are going to die? Is the team shot from the trailer real or fake? Let us know your thoughts in the comments!

articles.title: Why New Wave Music Won’t Go Away: New Documentary Explores How Synthesizers, MTV and Androgyny Built the Enduring Genre
articles.summary: From “Stranger Things” to virtually any Trader Joe’s, new wave music is inescapable. Not only are bands like B-52s, Duran Duran, Tears for Fears and Billy Idol still frequently touring, new generations are embracing the danceable sounds of 1977 to 1987, whether the tunes are making shoppers dance at your local Trader Joe's or soundtracking […]
articles.content:
From “Stranger Things” to virtually any Trader Joe’s, new wave music is inescapable. Not only are bands like B-52s , Duran Duran, Tears for Fears and Billy Idol still frequently touring, new generations are embracing the danceable sounds of 1977 to 1987, whether the tunes are making shoppers dance at your local Trader Joe's or soundtracking a nostalgia-tinged TV series.

How has the genre managed to hang on for so long, even as rock is no longer the dominant sound across the music scene? The new docuseries “New Wave,” premiering Monday on MGM+, tells the story of how a loosely connected group of misfits, fashionistas and punk rockers from the U.K. and U.S. coalesced to form a movement — and how the dawn of music videos then propelled that music into the stratosphere. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Cannes Condemns Five-Year Prison Sentence Against Iranian Palme d’Or Winner Jafar Panahi and Pleads for International Support Seville European Film Festival Honors Agnieszka Holland, Thierry Frémaux and Cartoon Saloon

In the doc, musicians, DJs and veejays (Martha Quinn! Mark Goodman!) consider the ingredients that created the movement: the influence of women, the colorful and original fashions of the era and the dawn of MTV, all coming together to create a joyful decade of energetic music that still resonates today.

Interviews in the four-part series include Kate Pierson and Fred Schneider of the B52s, Billy Idol, Mark Mothersbaugh of Devo, Danny Elfman of Oingo Boingo, Stewart Copeland of the Police, John Taylor of Duran Duran, Curt Smith of Tears for Fears, Johnny Marr of the Smiths, Kathy Valentine of the Go-Gos, Brian Setzer of Stray Cats and Jim Kerr of Simple Minds.

New wave torchbearer Richard Blade, the KROQ and Sirius First Wave DJ who has helped keep fans engaged with the sound ever since it started, serves as consulting producer, with Douglas Tirola directing. R.J. Cutler and Elise Pearlstein are among the executive producers. The production company is This Machine Filmworks, a part of Sony Pictures Television. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Speaking with Variety , the B52s' Pierson and the creative team broke down how new wave got started and labeled, how the series was put together and why the music has endured so long.

Douglas Tirola: The idea was that by telling this story, we would sort of defend new wave. I think a lot of people think of it as a keyboard, two people, a synthesizer, and a band from Britain making quirky dance music. It’s so much more than that. New wave brought the alternative into the mainstream. It changed music, movies, TV, design, fashion, politics, and how we look at and go out with one another.

Everybody loves the music of their youth; it’s their soundtrack, and it’s nostalgic to them. I felt there was a belief system behind New Wave, and that’s what the story set out to show.

Elise Pearlstein: New Wave was a short period — really only about 10 years — but so much music was created and the culture changed during that time. There had never really been a documentary that looked specifically at new wave, so we all thought it was high time.

Pearlstein: It was really a marketing term. New wave artists were originally grouped with punk, and punk wasn’t commercial. Some venues didn’t want punk acts to play because they would destroy the place. So “new wave” was a marketing term created to distinguish new wave artists from the punk movement and, ultimately, make them more commercially viable. And it worked.

Kate Pierson: I really think it’s a made-up term trying to encompass post-punk. Punk was just evolving; this was a sort of evolution from punk. The whole idea was that you could express yourself in any way, and anyone could do it. I think the thing about new wave that changed from punk was that it was inclusive. There were a lot more women, queer artists and Black artists in the scene.

Having a mixed band, with queer men and women in it, made us very different and unique in that scene. But it really fit into the whole new-wave fashion: it was fashion-forward and had eclectic influences. There was also technology — the addition of synthesizers and electronic music. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Every band was so different from the others. New wave embraced all these different styles: danceable music, funky music, even some disco influences. We loved disco.

Tirola: There were more people running around with video cameras, even if they were big. With the explosion of cable, more people were producing content, even if it was cable access. That was a relief. Once you hit the ’80s, there’s a lot more out there.

R.J. Cutler: It coincides with the arrival of MTV, which was a great gift to the filmmakers.

Pearlstein: A lot of the bands came from art school. Talking Heads and the B-52s were interested in visual media and the visual medium, so they embraced visual storytelling around music. Even before making music videos, bands like Devo were playing around with film and visuals in their music.

Pierson: The ripped garbage-bag look that Belinda Carlisle wore, or Debbie Harry’s style — it was this fusion of punk, avant-garde style and thrift-store chic. It was very “anything goes” and experimental fashion, which was so great.

I think we (the B-52s) made an impact visually, so MTV embraced us, and that helped a lot.

Pearlstein: Because it’s a pretty tight chronology — it’s only a 10-year period — we looked at the arc of new wave. It went from obscurity to a pretty fast demise within that time. We looked at how it broke out and became mainstream, how it peaked and jumped the shark, and then how it dissipated.

We also looked at milestones, like the synthesizer, which democratized the ability to make this kind of music, and MTV. Bob Geldof’s Band Aid and Live Aid were important moments when everybody came together, and you saw the diversity of the music as well as its commitment to change.

Then new wave started showing up in ads and getting co-opted by the mainstream. Ultimately, it was parodied. Once it got too extreme, some artists, like U2, didn’t want to be associated with new wave; they wanted to be beyond a genre. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Cutler: The fundamental story of outsiders becoming insiders is a great landscape for dramatic storytelling.

Tirola: Richard Blade was an absolute resource throughout this entire thing. He helped us get some of the interviews, gave us information, and gave us some of the key plot points. One point was when new wave took off. Richard talked about three songs that came out in a short period of time. One was Gary Numan’s “Cars.” I’d never put those three songs together that way before.

New wave took the place of disco. Then, when some things didn’t work out, the industry said, “No, we don’t want New Wave,” and then it had a comeback.

Tirola: I thought John Taylor was incredible. He said during the interview, “Thank God someone’s finally making this.” (Kate Pierson) also understood what new wave was: it was for outsiders, but outsiders who wanted to be in the mainstream. Every interview was great, but that one was special. Billy Idol, who I was a fan of but had never met, was so insightful and detail-oriented. He understood the bigger idea we were going for: where new wave fits into the big picture.

Tirola: U2 comes to mind. I feel like Bono and their early story would have been interesting. I think people forget they weren’t always a stadium band.

Richard Blade: When U2 played at the US Festival, they were a small band. If you look at the running order, they opened for Missing Persons. Bono went to climb the speaker stacks and wave his rebel flag, as he liked to do at concerts, and security grabbed his leg and pulled him down: “What do you think you’re doing? Get down from there!” Back then, he was just this scruffy little Irish guy trying to climb the speaker stacks. It’s amazing to see them go from that to perhaps the biggest rock band in the world

Blade: The younger generation is growing up with it now because it’s been used so many times in commercials. If you watch an NFL game, every third commercial — if it’s not Peyton Manning selling something — has an ’80s song playing. “Stranger Things” was the perfect example of that, and so many shows followed its influence on the ’80s. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It’s not just the parents, and it’s not going to fade away as we get older. People will continue to love Depeche Mode, The Cure and Duran Duran, just as people love the Beatles, The Who, The Beach Boys and The Rolling Stones.

Pearlstein: The B-52s really epitomize that (staying power). The music is fun, danceable, hopeful, sticky, addictive — and it makes you feel good.

I also think 20-somethings today have rediscovered New Wave in a huge way. The gender fluidity new wave embraced is back today, and the sounds, looks, and goth style are all popular again.

Cutler: It captures the spirit of youth forever. For those of us whose youth it’s tied to, it’s always resonant, but there’s also a timelessness to its spirit of rebellion and inclusion. The combination makes it forever young, and that’s really exciting.

It’s still driving culture.

(This interview has been edited and condensed.)

articles.title: Dark New Zombie Anime Confirms January 2027 Release Date Ahead of Debut
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Frontier Engine One of the most anticipated horror anime of 2027 confirms its release date and Japanese broadcast information with a new visual. 2026 is almost nearing its end, which is why the next year's lineup is revealing all the major information fans can expect. 2027 is going to be yet another exciting year for anime fans, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the most anticipated horror anime of 2027 confirms its release date and Japanese broadcast information with a new visual. 2026 is almost nearing its end, which is why the next year's lineup is revealing all the major information fans can expect. 2027 is going to be yet another exciting year for anime fans, maybe even better than this year. The year will kick off with the Winter 2027 season, which is only a few weeks away. One of the most exciting anime of the season is In a World Full of Zombies I'm the Only One Who Doesn't Get Attacked , a zombie horror series.

There has been a shortage of zombie movies in the industry for quite some time, even though Zom 100: Bucket List of the Dead was quite a massive hit in 2023. However, this new zombie series is expected to be the next big hit. The official X handle of the anime confirmed that AT-X on Friday, January 1, 2027, at 1:00 a.m. JST. The streaming platform hasn't been revealed yet, but we can expect an update before the end of the year. Along with the broadcast information, the handle post also includes an older visual featuring the central characters.

The anime is based on a light novel series of the same name written by Rokuro Uraji and illustrated by Saburo. The story centers around an ordinary office worker, Yusuke, who dislikes people and prefers to do his job in silence. However, when the company he was employed at goes bankrupt, he loses his job and becomes a shut-in with no motivation to work again. On a rare day, he leaves his apartment after playing video games for a week but never expected a mysterious man to bite his arm.

While Yusuke avoids getting hurt anymore, he becomes bedridden with a fever, never expecting the world would change when he was asleep. He sees that zombies have emerged in every corner of the world and only a few humans have survived the apocalypse. For some reason, he is the only one who isn't getting attacked by zombies, and it might be related to his unexpected encounter with the man who bit him.

A zombie apocalypse is one of those premises that fans will always love, especially those who have been starving for a horror genre. With the anime being oversaturated with battle action that centers around supernatural power systems or isekai fantasies, horror shows have become quite a rarity. This is especially the case for shows centering around Zombies since the last time a major hit was released was more than three years ago.

Not only that, but this upcoming series also comes with its own set of mysteries and plot twists that set it apart from any ordinary horror show. The anime has yet to reveal any information regarding its global streaming, but we can expect any major platform such as Crunchyroll, Netflix, or HIDIVE to pick it up soon.

articles.summary: Taylor Swift has gone on record from early in her teens forward as a Brenda Lee fan, and on her recent trip to Nashville she got to honor her predecessor in country-pop crossover stardom with a plaque honoring the diamond-selling status of Lee's "Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree." Only two Christmas singles have been certified […]
articles.content:
Taylor Swift has gone on record from early in her teens forward as a Brenda Lee fan, and on her recent trip to Nashville she got to honor her predecessor in country-pop crossover stardom with a plaque honoring the diamond-selling status of Lee's "Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree."

Only two Christmas singles have been certified by the RIAA for selling 10 million copies, with Lee's 1958 signature smash becoming the second, following Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Chasing Summer' Director Josephine Decker Says That ‘Filmmaking Is Lonelier Than Ever,’ So It’s Time to Build a Community

A video posted on Instagram shows Swift knocking on the door to a room where the 81-year-old Lee is awaiting a visitor. "No way," Lee says, upon first being greeted. "You grow a foot?" Swift responds, "One per year, yeah."

Getting to the matter at hand, Swift says, " I'm one of the many, many fans of your iconic song 'Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree.' It is such an incredible song. And I'm not the only person who feels that way, because I'm very honored to get to present you with your diamond certification for more than 10 million copies. You recorded this when you were only 13 years old, and it is one of only two Christmas songs to ever reach this milestone. You're in very good company with Mariah Carey, all the way at the top, and this is yours now, and it will be yours forever… On behalf of all the fans and all the families and people whose Christmases this song has absolutely added dazzle and sparkle and warmth to, thank you so much for your incredible work."

Lee immediately thinks of collaborators who are not around to join the celebration. "Well, the writer, Johnny Marks, who's no longer here, would be so proud. And all the musicians and (producer) Owen Bradley, everybody, all the fans…" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"I'm so happy to get to have this moment with you," Swift says, noting she has "been such a fan for so long." "And I'm a fan," responds Lee. "Oh, really?" "Yes. I wish you wasn't so tall," says Lee, who at the so-called height of her fame, when she was known as "Little Miss Dynamite," stood at 4 feet 9 inches.

When she was 18, Swift wrote an essay about Lee, titled "Rare Peer." It was republished in a 2017 book in which female country artists saluted their heroes, the Holly Gleason-edited “Woman Walk the Line.”

articles.title: Protect Yourself from AI by Bidding on Terminator 2's Complete T-800 SFX Ensemble - Just Be Careful It Doesn't Terminate Your Wallet

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It is hard to find a part of society that AI has not found its way into over the last couple of years. From call centers to medical research and, of course, entertainment, the world has very quickly become a place where discussions about the use of thinking computers in daily life are always present. However, there are some who still think of AI as one of humanity's biggest threats thanks to the many sci-fi movies that have predicted dystopian futures when machines rise against the human race. Perhaps the best way to counter this is to have your own futuristic robot on hand to protect you, and who better than Arnold Schwarzenegger's T-800 from the Terminator movies . Although the character was the villain of James Cameron's 1984 movie, he returned several years later in Terminator 2: Judgment Day as the good guy. Now, thanks to Prop Store , you could own your own production used Terminator.

For fans of the Terminator franchise, this is as close as you can hope to get to one of Skynet's robots. The lot in Prop Store's winter auction features Schwarzenegger's full iconic costume with an electronic head created by special effects master Stan Winston's studio for the movie. For collectors who want to own a Terminator grail piece to really show off to your friends, then there can be nothing better than having one on guard at the door. The only thing is, you are going to need a very deep wallet if you plan on bidding as this thing comes with a price tag that hits harder than a T-1000. While the starting bid on the full ensemble is $30,000, the high-end estimate is $120,000, and based on some recent memorabilia auctions it could sell for even higher if two people decide they want to battle it out to win it.

There are plenty of movies that can be called memorable, but when Terminator 2: Judgment Day blasted into cinemas in 1991 it became a true landmark in filmmaking for its visionary director James Cameron . The highest grossing movie of the year with a box office that soared over $500 million, Cameron's epic sequel to his low-budget hit original also won several Academy Awards for its incredible makeup and effects. While many were massively impressed by the early use of computer-generated effects that brought the T-1000's liquid metal state to life, the prosthetics, animatronics, and life-like replicas of Schwarzenegger used to show his battle-damaged T-800 were so impressive that they still hold up incredibly well today.

The Terminator has become one of the most instantly recognisable action characters in cinema history, with Cameron's genius idea to turn his unstoppable villain into the franchise's hero on his second outing stopping Terminator 2 being just another sequel that repeats what has gone before . Of course, that is what James Cameron does, and it is why he is behind three of the highest-grossing movies of all time. It is perhaps then not surprising that owning any piece of a Cameron movie would be a dream come true for many, so this auction for an actual Terminator is one that will draw a lot of attention by the time the hammer falls on December 4. While Cameron has hinted that he could be thinking of dipping back into the Terminator franchise again with a new movie, it would be without the legendary T-800. Yet, anytime you hear the word Terminator, there is only one image that comes instantly to mind, and who knows, owning it may even grant you favor with the AI gods when they finally decide to take over the planet .

Is Terminator 2 the best sequel ever made? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: For Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, 'Cliff Booth' Closes Out a Massive Year in Wild Style
articles.summary: The Emmy winner makes a meal of his supporting role in David Fincher's anticipated stand-alone sequel, which should come as no surprise: The actor has been delivering memorable performances all year long.
articles.content:
It’s the kind of year an actor dreams of — prestige award nominations preceded by big-screen action showcases, juicy leading roles followed by scene-stealing supporting parts. And for Yahya Abdul-Mateen II , it’s not even over — the New Orleans native’s fourth screen credit of the year, David Fincher ’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , is out in IMAX theaters on Wednesday.

“This is a fantastic year,” as Abdul-Mateen puts it in the first of two chats we’ve had over the last few months. “None of those characters are in conversation with one another. They're from completely different worlds.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV 'The Body' Breakout Geena Meszaros on Finding Empathy for Lisbeth and "Life-Altering" Female Friendships TV Netflix Renews Japanese Crime Hit 'Tokyo Swindlers' for Season 2

To put it mildly, we knew Abdul-Mateen was good for it. Breaking out by anchoring the box-office hit Candyman and winning an Emmy for his soulful turn in HBO’s Watchmen , his range and ability to swerve between different scopes of characters has been evident for years. His 2026 started with the MCU entry Wonder Man , which was canceled after a single season despite strong reviews and viewership — and which earned the actor his first lead-acting Emmy nod, for a turn that showed off his comedic chops. He then led the latest Man on Fire adaptation for Netflix , which topped the streamer’s viewership charts out of its debut, and Paramount’s original theatrical play By Any Means , Elegance Bratton’s incendiary historical thriller set in the Deep South.

articles.title: Donald Trump Puts Himself At Center Of Jensen Huang's Reinstatement, Downplays "Sex Sells" Scandal Amid National Security Concerns

articles.content:
After a whirlwind of a morning of news coverage on the bombshell reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO, Donald Trump posted a photo to his Truth Social account, replacing his image following the 2024 assassination attempt with that of the leader of the AI giant.

In the doctored photo, it is Huang waving his fist, and holding a red brassiere, a reference to the scandal in which the CEO was involved in an alleged honeytrap affair with a woman alleged to have connections to Chinese spy operations.

"Sex sells," Trump told CNBC in a phone call to the network about an hour earlier, pretty much dismissing Huang's indiscretion as an extramarital affair and downplaying national security concerns. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News Democratic National Committee Plans 12 Presidential Primary Debates Starting In June News Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang As CEO

As much as Trump had been urging Huang to be reinstated in recent days, the dramatic announcement of Huang's return still seemed to surprise news media.

On CNBC, just before 9 a.m. ET, anchors warned the control room not to go to a commercial break as the Nvidia announcement came across. Then they could be heard reacting to the news with expressions of "woohoo" and "unbelievable."

About a half hour earlier, PBS News ' Liz Landers had talked to Trump, who seemingly spilled the beans on the announcement to come by telling her that Huang is "back where he should be." Trump would not comment, though, on a New York Times report on Monday that Huang's mistress, Alice Huang, was in contact with an official with China 's top spy agency for more than a year as she had an affair with the tech titan.

What is clear is that Trump has placed himself at the center of Huang's reinstatement, embracing him not just as an essential CEO but, with the cheeky Truth Social imagery, a fellow victim of circumstance.

Undoubtedly, Trump was alarmed by what was happening to the market slide into dear territory, and the reinstatement decision has so far elevated Nvidia's stock price by more than 30%. In his CNBC interview, Trump did not confirm that he was on the Nvidia board call but said that he was "represented" there, representing an unusual intervention by the White House in a private company's corporate governance. Trump said that he have the board "enough assurance" about Huang, having posted on Truth Social earlier that "the United States government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to Nvidia poses any risk to national security." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

While Trump predicted that Huang would return to the company with a performance "at an almost higher level," the scrutiny on the CEO and the White House itself may only intesify in the coming weeks, even with Republicans still in control of Congress through the end of the year. Huang is still scheduled to testify before to House committees next month.

Sen. John Curtis (R-UT) wrote on X, "Nvidia’s board says it relied on input from senior U.S. officials to conclude that bringing Jensen Huang back posed no national security risk. I have some questions. Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?"

Other lawmakers promised to pursue investigations, raising the "what did the president know, and when did he know it?" types of Watergate-era questions.

Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD), set to become the chair of the House Judiciary Committee in the next Congress, said the Trump had been briefed "about the facts as early as last year," while noting Trump's holdings in Nvidia stock. Raskin said in a statement, "Why are Trump and [Commerce Secretary Howard] Lutnick putting China's interests first? Is it just the tens and hundreds of millions of dollars they’re making out in the open or does Huang have even more damning information on them? A real Congress will find out."

Even Newt Gingrich, the former House speaker and Trump supporter, found the circumstances troubling.

He wrote on X, "There is something profoundly wrong about Jensen Huang having a relationship with a Chinese Communist Spy and helping China get a huge number of very advanced computer chips when that was specifically against the policy of the United States Government and now he is being reinstated as ceo of the most advanced chip making company in the world. Congress should really dig into this as a national security issue of enormous proportions and also a significant failure in the federal bureaucracy."

articles.title: One Way Jimmy Fallon Is Differentiating Himself From Jimmy Kimmel This Holiday TV Season
articles.summary: Late-night TV lovers will have a solid meal on Turkey Day.
articles.content:
Thanksgiving is nearly upon us and, with that, avid TV viewers can look forward to plenty of programming specifically geared towards the holiday. As all of those special offerings roll in on network TV, some may be wondering what’s going on with the late-night shows. There are now details regarding what hosts Jimmy Fallon , Jimmy Kimmel and Seth Meyers have planned for this coming week. And, from the looks of it, Fallon is differentiating himself from Kimmel over the holidays in a very keen way.

NBC – which houses both The Tonight Show and Late Night with Seth Meyers – has long capitalized on Turkey Day. After all, the storied network remains the home of the beloved Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade (which Fallon has participated in) . Historically, Fallon and Meyers’ shows have sought to draw in viewers even on the night of the holiday, and that’ll continue this year. Both shows will be on for T-giving amid the 2026 TV schedule , and they have some special developments planned.

Per NBC’s press site, Fallon’s Tonight Show will kick off the week of November 23 with a repeat on Monday and then run new episodes from Tuesday to Thursday. When it comes to the Thanksgiving broadcast, Fallon is set to welcome back his old pal, Justin Timberlake, to the show for the first time in two years. Said episode could lead to some memorable moments as has been the case with past T-giving broadcasts. I’m sure some devoted viewers remember Fallon and Kevin James’ messy food sketch from 2016.

It definitely tracks that NBC would want to keep these late-night offerings on the air during Thanksgiving. Not only networks are alike, though, as it seems that Jimmy Kimmel and co. at ABC are going a different route.

The ABC press site confirms that Jimmy Kimmel Live ! will only air new episodes on Monday, November 23 and Tuesday, November 24. For the remainder of the week, the show will go on a break and reruns will air in its place. So, in other words, this marks a brief hiatus for the team over at Live! Of course, such a break isn’t unheard of for this show or any other like it. What’s also worth noting is that this break comes months after Kimmel’s latest time away from the desk.

Pratt plays Jake, a decorated Navy SEAL sidelined by injury and haunted by the loss of a comrade after a failed mission to rescue children taken hostage “by militants overseas.” Convalescing at the San Diego home of his sister Sarah (the infinitely more deserving Linda Cardellini), Jake aims to recover well enough to return to active duty and complete his mission. But when Sarah’s son Marc (Hill) begs him for training to stand up to schoolyard bully Kenny (Levi McConaughey), Jake agrees to put the kid on an exercise regimen — with the provision that Marc also learns how to avoid fighting altogether.

As a kid who can’t walk from his front door to the school bus without tripping on his own shoelaces, Marc thrills at the chance to develop a bit of muscle, along with some much-needed confidence. But as Marc faces his fears for the first time, Jake’s stiff-upper-lipped attitude to his own pain quickly melts in the warming glow of the pair’s camaraderie. As Jake eyes another tour of duty to go back and finish what he started, Marc begins to realize that prevailing over his tormentor doesn’t have to mean the physical fight he’s been preparing for all summer. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Willink has thus far written five books about Marc and his uncle Jake, so there is clearly an appetite for stories that are both family-friendly and military-adjacent. But condensed to an overlong 106 minutes of screen time, this adaptation of the first in the series treads an awkward line between elements that kids can take away from watching, and those directed at their parents (or uncles).

Marc is a kid who loves video games and feels particularly empowered playing a Rock Band stand-in called Band Jam; each time he plays, McG cleverly transforms the world around him to reflect his sense of empowerment. Gen X-ers like Jake, with or without intense military training, will likely have little tolerance for the boy’s preferred method of athletic activity — which is to say, through a gaming console — but Jake seldom meets his nephew at his level, instead instructing him on warrior values, never translating the boy’s interest from the virtual world to the real one.

As Staples’ script efficiently reveals, Marc’s own father has passed away, prompting Jake to respond, “Okay, that happened.” It's meant not as a dismissal, but to encourage Marc to move on from the kind of identity-defining loss that lurks in just about everyone’s background, including Jake's. But 40 years ago, Mr. Miyagi in “The Karate Kid” taught audiences to apply the deeper lesson from a superficial act, and everything here is terribly literal, making it less relatable to a broader spectrum of adolescents who might gain some real perspective from this tale.

It’s hard to know if Pratt is trying to prove, post-“Guardians of the Galaxy,” that he’s more than a buffoon, or if he’s injecting his signature goofy humor into characters, like Jack, who are meant to be more serious and capable. But this character is an uncomfortable and frequently joyless fit for the guy whose golden-retriever energy elevated Andy Dwyer from comic relief to an essential part of the ensemble on “Parks and Recreation.” Good-looking guys can be funny, but the more fit and conventionally handsome Pratt gets, the less interesting his performances become.

"Belfast" star Hill seems talented, but it’s hard to know if he’s been given line readings here by his director, or if someone has guided him to act “like an adult” in his performance, turning it into a pantomime of awkward adolescence. Cardellini, meanwhile, frantically fights against all the movie clichés of single motherhood — well-meaning and devoted but frazzled — but the movie is so focused on the relationship between Jake and Marc that there’s not much room for her deeply felt work. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Assuming Staples’ script translates Willink’s book faithfully, the author is to be commended for not simply lapsing into teenage wish-fulfillment and letting Marc teach Kenny a well-needed lesson. But what McG does instead is offer a much bigger, more elaborate and less plausible opportunity for Marc to triumph, which takes the film from the realm of reality — albeit one where foreign militants will wait weeks for the soldier trying to stop them to recover from his injuries — to a sequence from “Spy Kids.” The film is most winning when it's most grounded — as when it puts the audience in Marc’s shoes, using the camera to make him feel disembodied as he gingerly asks his dream girl on a date.

Ultimately, Pratt is too big a star to simply act in support of a story where he isn’t the focus — which ends up being to the detriment of what is really a kid's tale. Because the film must cater to his movie-star presence, the epiphanies experienced by Marc feel designed for adults to appreciate, offering a pointed reminder that there’s a difference between not talking down to a kid and not talking directly to one. “Way of the Warrior Kid” doesn't bring enjoyment, empowerment or enlightenment, so much as a sense of, "Okay, that happened.” Either way, a sock in the teeth feels as appropriate a response to somebody throwing your bike into San Diego Bay as spending an entire summer building a psychological profile understanding why they threw it in there in the first place.

The American Film Institute established its first full-ride scholarship dedicated to production design.

The AFI World Builder Scholarship for Production Design will be awarded to an admitted fall 2027 Production Design Fellow and cover tuition across the four-semester, full-time program.

“The AFI Conservatory has championed visual storytellers and worldbuilders for nearly 60 years, empowering thousands of filmmakers to express their unique vision,” said Susan Ruskin, Dean of the AFI Conservatory. “We’re thrilled to expand our scholarship opportunities with the first-ever AFI World Builder Scholarship for Production Design, highlighting the invaluable artistic contribution of production designers who create stunning visuals and transport audiences to new worlds.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Chasing Summer' Director Josephine Decker Says That ‘Filmmaking Is Lonelier Than Ever,’ So It’s Time to Build a Community

The AFI Conservatory hosted a conversation with production design alumni as part of the announcement. Tom Hammock (AFI Class of 2004, “Weapons,” “Resident Evil”) and Claudia Ethridge (AFI Class of 2018, “Euphoria,” “The SpongeBob Movie: Search for SquarePants”) discussed why they pursued production design as a career, their experience at the Conservatory and their advice for aspiring filmmakers.

“It really is this amazing place where independent filmmaking and studio filmmaking come together and prepare you to take either path and go off into the world and really try and create worlds for films to take place in," Hammock said.

articles.title: The Sony INZONE M10S II Offers Stunning OLED Visuals in a Surprisingly Small Package (Review)
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Sony Sometimes, a new piece of gaming hardware makes you stop playing for a moment just to appreciate what you're looking at. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Sometimes, a new piece of gaming hardware makes you stop playing for a moment just to appreciate what you're looking at. Effectively, that's what happened when I started using the Sony INZONE M10S II. I was immediately struck by how vibrant everything looked. Colors practically leap off the screen, giving everything from sprawling landscapes to the smallest visual details a level of richness that I haven't personally experienced on a gaming monitor before. After experiencing some of gaming's most recent visually striking releases on the display, I came away with one pretty clear impression: Sony has made something special here.

The INZONE M10S II is a premium gaming monitor with some seriously impressive performance specifications, but its picture quality is what really won me over from the moment I powered it up. It's also remarkably slim and lightweight, which is a welcome change from the bulky displays that can make a desk feel like it's running out of room. I do have a couple of reservations, but they didn't take away from how much I enjoyed using it.

The first thing I noticed about the INZONE M10S II was just how good everything looked. I've used plenty of gaming monitors over the years, so it takes a lot for a new display to genuinely surprise me. This one managed it almost immediately. The colors are incredibly rich without making the image feel overdone, and environments have a vibrancy that makes you want to stop and take everything in. It doesn't change the way you play a game, but it can absolutely make you enjoy looking at one a whole lot more.

I tested the monitor with several different games, including the new Crimson Desert DLC , Phantom Blade Zero , and Enshrouded : a pretty varied collection of art styles and environments. I'm happy to report that the INZONE M10S II handled all three beautifully. The sweeping scenery and colorful environments of Crimson Desert looked particularly fantastic, while the striking visual effects in Phantom Blade Zero had plenty of room to shine. Even the distinct presentation of Enshrouded benefited from the display's excellent color reproduction. No matter what I was playing, I found myself appreciating just how much the monitor brought to the image.

A big part of that experience comes down to the monitor's OLED panel. Unlike traditional LCD displays that rely on a backlight, OLED pixels illuminate individually, allowing the screen to produce deep blacks and impressive contrast. It helps bright colors stand out even more against darker surroundings. The M10S II also supports 99.5% DCI-P3 color coverage, giving it a wide color gamut that helps explain the richness I noticed during my testing. With HDR support adding another dimension to compatible content, there's plenty here to appreciate beyond simply having a high-end gaming display. This is the sort of picture quality that makes going back to an ordinary monitor just a bit harder.

Of course, there's more to the INZONE M10S II than making games look pretty. Sony has packed this monitor with specifications aimed squarely at competitive gaming in collaboration with E-Sports team, Fnatic. Its QHD resolution runs at up to 540Hz, while a separate dual-mode option can push the refresh rate to 720Hz at a reduced 720p resolution. The panel also boasts a 0.02ms response time, making it an exceptionally fast display on paper.

This detail specifically appealing to players who spend their time in competitive shooters, where quick reactions and clear motion can make a difference. That said, I don't want to pretend that I spent my testing period chasing refresh-rate records. My experience with the monitor was much more focused on enjoying the games I was playing, and the image quality consistently delivered. The high-end specifications are certainly welcome, but I suspect the pristine visual presentation will be what most people remember after using it.

The physical design is another area where Sony deserves praise. Gaming monitors can be surprisingly bulky, especially when you factor in their stands and the space they occupy on a desk. The INZONE M10S II takes a much more restrained approach. It's incredibly thin and noticeably lighter than the monitors I'm accustomed to using, making it far easier to reposition when necessary. I appreciate hardware that doesn't make moving things around my setup feel like an entire project, and this monitor fits that preference perfectly. It's a premium display that doesn't demand an equally massive footprint.

It's also refreshingly straightforward to get started. I didn't feel the need to spend ages digging through settings or experimenting with calibration before I could enjoy what was on screen. I connected it, got everything running, and started playing. That's exactly the sort of experience I want from a premium gaming monitor. There are plenty of customization options available for those who want to fine-tune their display, but I was perfectly happy with the picture straight out of the box. Sometimes, the best feature is not having to spend your first hour with a new monitor figuring out how to make it look good.

Despite how much I enjoyed using the INZONE M10S II, there is one aspect of its design that I struggled to get past: the size. Sony markets the display as a 27-inch monitor, which is certainly enough room to enjoy games, and the quality of the OLED panel goes a long way toward making up for the relatively compact screen. Still, I've grown accustomed to larger displays, and once you're used to gaming on something above 30 inches, moving back down can feel like a noticeable downgrade.

It's not that the M10S II is difficult to enjoy because of its dimensions. Quite the opposite. The picture is so impressive that I rarely found myself thinking about the screen size while actually playing. But when I stepped back and considered what I would want from a permanent gaming setup, I found myself wishing Sony had gone a little bigger. For competitive players who prefer a smaller display, that may actually be a benefit. For someone like me, however, it's the biggest compromise. It's a little frustrating to have such a gorgeous picture and still find yourself wishing there were more of it.

Then there's the price. With an MSRP of $1,099.99, the INZONE M10S II is an expensive piece of gaming hardware. Sony's US store listing currently places it for $999.99, a $100 discount from that MSRP. That's still a substantial investment for a 27-inch QHD monitor, even one with an OLED panel and some seriously impressive performance specifications. You're paying for a premium display with technology designed to appeal to competitive players, and the quality certainly reflects that. But I wouldn't blame anyone for taking a moment to consider whether they really need everything this monitor offers before spending that much money. As much as I enjoyed using it, this isn't exactly an impulse purchase.

The Sony INZONE M10S II made a fantastic impression on me. Its vibrant OLED display brought every game I tested to life, and I genuinely enjoyed seeing just how much color and detail it could deliver. The incredibly slim construction is another major selling point, especially for anyone who wants a premium gaming monitor without adding another bulky piece of hardware to their desk. Most importantly, I never felt like I needed to jump through hoops to get the experience I wanted. Plug it in, fire up a game, and enjoy. It's a wonderfully straightforward experience, backed by a display that really knows how to make an impression.

I do wish the display were a little larger, and its asking price is undeniably steep. Those are meaningful considerations, particularly when there are plenty of gaming monitors available for considerably less. Still, the INZONE M10S II delivers an experience that's difficult to argue with. If you're looking to invest in a high-end gaming monitor and put visual quality near the top of your priorities, Sony has made something special here. It's an easy recommendation, and one of the most visually impressive monitors I've had the pleasure of testing.

A loaner of this product was provided to ComicBook.com for the purpose of this review.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus is a newly enhanced version of the now classic TV anime series, and with the benefit of […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Dragon Ball Super 's new remake has officially kicked off the Resurrection F arc with its latest episode, and Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has also planted the first seeds for Ultra Instinct Goku's big debut. Dragon Ball Super: Beerus is a newly enhanced version of the now classic TV anime series, and with the benefit of retrospect has been able to fine tune how each of the episodes play out knowing what's next to come in the future. That's what makes its newest addition all the more interesting.

Dragon Ball Super fans know that the anime eventually reaches its climax with the full debut of Mastered Ultra Instinct Goku , and Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has been able to use that to start planting the seeds for it much sooner than usual. Because while the anime hasn't really changed any of the audio or story sequences from the original, it's been able to add a new visual flourish to help set up Ultra Instinct's eventually debut with the latest episode.

Whis explains Ultra Instinct to Goku and Vegeta pic.twitter.com/QD4NnJnbRg

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Episode 7 kicks off the Resurrection F arc with Goku and Vegeta training with Whis on Beerus' planet . This training segment is extended beyond what was seen in the original version as well as the conversation that Whis has with the two of them about their strengths and weaknesses. When Whis tells them they will need to train their body to move before they even think of those movements, the new version now adds a flair of silver aura that wasn't in the original. It's because now the team knows what Ultra Instinct already looks like.

Rather than like the first time around where the Dragon Ball Super anime production team were kind of figuring things out alongside Akira Toriyama as the series developed, Dragon Ball Super: Beerus is able to use those future events to foreshadow them much sooner than before. It makes for a more complete experience for those new audiences who are just jumping into the anime with this new edition, and will hopefully make Ultra Instinct that much more explosive if/when the remake eventually gets to the Tournament of Power.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has only been confirmed to enhance the Battle of Gods, Resurrection F and Universe 6 arcs before it comes to an end. It's yet to be revealed as to whether or not the Future Trunks and Universe Survival arcs are going to get the remake treatment next, but that seems likely given that these three arcs have gone through the trouble of being reinterpreted in this way. That's going to be even more necessary to bridge the gap to the Dragon Ball Super: The Galactic Patrol anime at some point too.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus has been divisive thus far with the number of changes it has made to the classic TV anime, and the lack of new additions seen with the episodes so far . But with foreshadowing like this to help make the package seemed like it was all planned out from the start, it's going to make this new version the most complete version of the story. articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Just Teased the End of the Multiverse, And You Probably Missed It
articles.summary: Marvel Studios Avengers: Doomsday's final trailer is out, and the internet is buzzing about just how much more of the film it has revealed. Rumors have proven to be true: Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) is at the heart of the multiversal calamity that has Earths of every different reality crashing into one another in a mass incursion. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday 's final trailer is out, and the internet is buzzing about just how much more of the film it has revealed. Rumors have proven to be true: Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) is at the heart of the multiversal calamity that has Earths of every different reality crashing into one another in a mass incursion. The heroes of the main Marvel Cinematic Universe, the Fantastic Four's alternate version of the MCU, and the Fox X-Men movie universe will all need to fight for their respective worlds, while also forming tenuous alliances with one another, to combat the threat of Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr.).

The new Avengers: Doomsday trailer teases bigger stakes than ever for this film. However, there is one moment in the trailer that teases the final phase of Doomsday's crossover battle for multiversal survival – though not every viewer will likely recognize the moment when they see it.

The new Avengers: Doomsday trailer shows Steve Rogers reconciling with his decision to alter the MCU timeline and reunite with his love, Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell), at the end of Avengers: Endgame . Steve leaves Peggy and his son to rejoin the Avengers and Fantastic Four. At about 1:31 in the trailer, we see Steve looking at the skyline of New York City from what is (presumably) Avengers Tower: in the sky are two other worlds, with one already looking like it is badly damaged, if not in the process of total collapse.

So what does this image mean? Well, previous films and TV shows in the MCU Multiverse Saga ( Loki , Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness ) have shown us that it looks pretty much like what you see below when two different realities of the multiverse crash into one another. The twist here is that we've never seen multiple worlds crash into one another, and this image suggests there are only three worlds left intact while the multiverse is in the final stages of annihilation.

That sets an (wait for it…) endgame for Doomsday 's second and third acts, where Earth-616 will presumably have split its forces into offensive and defensive squads. This trailer pretty much confirms who is on the offensive squad that goes to the X-Men's reality (Earth-10005) : Captain America (Anthony Mackie), Shang-Chi (Simu Liu), Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal), Thor (Chris Hemsworth) , and Yelena Belova (Florence Pugh).

What's interesting is that this trailer also suggests that characters like the rest of the Fantastic Four (Ben Grimm, Johnny and Sue Storm), Shuri (Letitia Wright) and the Wakandans, Namor, and the rest of the Thunderbolts (Bob, Red Guardian, Bucky, Ghost, U.S. Agent) could all be back on Earth-616 and having to battle some invaders who may or may not be connected to Doom. Sue is seen clearly trying to contain some power or force that pushes her power to the limit.

The story Avengers: Doomsday is crafting is certainly a tricky one to pull off. The nature of "heroism" doesn't seem to apply to this situation; for every team, "saving" their world now means killing other worlds. The audience has identified with every side of the conflict via the various film franchises we've enjoyed for over 25 years. It'll be hard for viewers to stay clearly oriented on who the "good" and "bad" guys are. That's especially true for Steve Rogers, who will go from being one of the biggest heroes of the Infinity Saga to the cause of the calamity in the Multiverse Saga. Hopefully the Russo Bros. have a smart way to refocus this all back on Doom as the main antagonist, and redeem all the heroes who need it (and survive).

Avengers: Doomsday will be in theaters on December 18th. What did you think of the trailer?

articles.content:
EXCLUSIVE: For years, Steven Spielberg has talked about how much he's wanted to direct a Western and it now looks like the three-time Oscar winner has found the perfect project to saddle up for. Sources tell Deadline, Spielberg is developing an untitled film for Focus Features and has assembled an all-star roster of A-list talent to bring it together. Jessie Buckley, Cillian Murphy and Mark Rylance are set to star in the film, directed by Spielberg from a script by Oscar winner Paul Thomas Anderson , based on Kevin Barry’s The Heart in Winter .

The film will come out some time in 2028 and follows two star-crossed fugitives trying to find a place for themselves in the American West. Kristie Macosko Krieger, Sarah Murphy, Anderson and Spielberg will produce the film. Tim Headington, Neil Shah, Ryan Zacarias, and Ana Leocha will executive produce. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News Indie Holiday Push: 'Minotaur', 'Elsinore' & 'Josephine' Debut With Cameron Winter Concert Film; 'Club Kid' Expands - Specialty Preview News Danny Boyle Talks 'Ink', The Common Architecture Of His Movies And More '28 Years Later' As He Receives The Deadline Legend Award

Spielberg spoke with Deadline about his decision to make this his first Western, and said not only did the story speak to him, but the opportunity to work with his longtime friend Anderson was too good to pass up. "It's really the excitement for me to get to work together with my dear friend and colleague Paul Thomas Anderson on a genre, but more particularly, the genre notwithstanding, a story that quite quickly became close to both our hearts and we felt that we could do as a team."

This will mark the first time Anderson has written something without directing it too, which just shows how much the Oscar-winning director wanted to work with Spielberg. Though many view Anderson more for his directing then writing, he is coming off an Oscar win for best adapted screenplay for One Battle After Another, a novel many believed was too tough of a story to adapt.

Spielberg said the two had begun talking about potentially working together since January and while they hadn't on this book since then, they very much wanted to make something set in America in the late 1800s.

"We've sat in screening rooms, and by the way, only on 35mm film, and watched dozens of Westerns," Spielberg added. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

As for the casting process, Spielberg said they were his top choices, and frankly Buckley and Murphy were "the only two actors that could play these characters."

"This story is about the people who refused to settle for a life that is less then they deserve but maybe more than they can handle," Spielberg said. "Jessie and Cillian were the first people to ever come to mind for this and they also have never made a film together."

Spielberg was also super excited at the idea of making the film at Focus Features after working with the studio on Hamnet, which he produced, and would land Buckley an Oscar for Best Actress at the 2026 Oscars.

"I'm really excited to be working with Kujo at Focus after doing Hamnet together, so it's a reunion in a sense for Jessie and it's also a reunion for PTA who did Phantom Thread at Focus Features," Spielberg said. "It's going to be a real hybrid production with Universal handling production, who will release through the Focus label, and both teams are going to work very closely with each other, which I'm very excited for as I know both worlds at Universal intimately."

Spielberg has a longstanding relationship with Universal Pictures and Focus Features. Most recently, Spielberg released Disclosure Day with Universal Pictures, which opened at No. 1 at the box office to critical acclaim. Spielberg also recently produced Hamnet for Focus Features, which received eight Oscar nominations, with Buckley winning Best Actress.

Spielberg added that his selections for below the line are still in process, but the plan is to shoot next year in the winter.

As for the question of whether this film was also a metaphor for his directing riding off into the sunset and making it his last film, not only is it not, but the iconic director has an idea of how he would want to do that when that day comes.

"If I wanted to ride off into the sunset, I would have done Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade next and I could have had those characters literally riding off into the sunset as the credits roll," Spielberg said.

Besides Hamnet, Buckley can be seen next in Three Incestuous Sisters, which also stars Saoirse Ronan, Dakota Johnson and Josh O'Connor. Murphy can be seen next in the new prison drama from Damien Chazelle that also stars Daniel Craig and Michelle Williams.

Prime Video ’s God of War video game adaptation has not gone on without some bumps in the road, but development on the show continues.

First eyed for a TV series adaptation by the producing studios in March 2022, the casting for the show gained momentum at the beginning of January 2026 after some creative shuffling.

For everything we know about Prime Video’s God of War adaptation, read on.

When will Prime Video’s God of War show come out? A date has not yet been set for the show’s release.

Is Prime Video’s God of War in production?

Yes, though the shoot had some complications when Ryan Hurst sustained a serious injury four months into shooting. Pre-production began at the end of 2025. The plan remains to film two seasons back to back. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Who is in the cast of Prime Video’s God of War show?

Ryan Hurst was originally cast as Kratos , the titular character of the video game. Kratos is a Spartan by birth and a god by nature, raised in martial culture. After rising in the ranks and commanding armies to protect his homeland, he made a fateful deal with the Greek God of War, Ares, exchanging his soul for being victorious in battle.

Following Hurst's tearing a bicep while performing a stunt during production in June, as first reported by TMZ, Deadline reported that the role of Kratos was being recast . Sony Pictures Television and Amazon MGM reached out to Dave Bautista to initiate talks shortly after they made the decision to recast the role.

Bautista, who is known for portraying Drax in the Guardians of the Galaxy film trilogy and for more recently voicing Tagah in Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender , closed his deal to take on the role in late August after reports that he was in talks started circulating at the beginning of the month.

Following Hurst’s casting as Kratos, Deadline broke the news that Teresa Palmer ( A Discovery of Witches , Warm Bodies ) was cast as Phoebe/Sif , wife of Thor and goddess of family. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Max Parker ( Boots ), will star as Heimdall , the Watchman of Asgard and one of Odin’s sons. Heimdall is a god in his own right, and he has the ability to anticipate what might happen in any moment. He’s constantly looking fore ways to improve his status and position in the hierarchy because he feels unappreciated by his father. Heimdall first appears in the second God of War game, God of War Ragnarök .

Ólafur Darri Ólafsson will portray Thor in the mythology-themed video game adaptation, as Deadline first reported. The God of Thunder is haunted by the price he paid in a war he fought long ago, making him a shadow of his former self who resorts to alcohol to escape what haunts him. He was once loyal to Asgard and his father’s right-hand man. He keeps his wife and children at arm’s length, further isolating himself, but his power lurks beneath the surface.

Ed Skrein ( Jurassic World Rebirth ) will portray Baldur , Odin’s youngest son and most dangerous weapon. Baldur was cursed as a boy, and the curse took away his ability to feel physical sensation and pleasure.

Deadline first reported Mandy Patinkin’s ( Homeland , The Princess Bride ) casting as Odin . Odin is the All-Father, or patriarch and most powerful Aesir god. He constantly seeks knowledge to prevent the prophecy of Ragnarök, or the Norse end of the world. He also presents an antagonist for Kratos.

Callum Vinson ( Chucky , Long Bright River ) will portray Atreus , the 10-year-old son of Kratos. Raised almost entirely by his mother Faye, Atreus grew up in a remote cabin, where he honed his archery skills and developed an affinity for animals. Things change, though, when he is left with his distant father, who he barely knows, after the death of his mother.

At the end of January 2026, Alastair Duncan ( God of War ,  God of War Ragnarök ) became the first voice actor from the video games to reprise their role in the Amazon MGM and Sony Pictures Television TV series. Duncan will portray cheery and chatty Mimir from Celtic lands. Jeff Gulka  ( The X-Files ,  Stargate SG-1 ) and Danny Woodburn ( The Witcher ,  Bookie ) are set to play brothers, Sindri and Brok , in recurring roles.

Towards the end of November 2026, Deborah Ann Woll was cast to reprise her role as Faye from the video game in the Prime Video series.

Sonya Walger ( For All Mankind ) will portray Freya , Vamir goddess and princess who wields ancient and powerful magic. She is Odin’s ex-wife and former queen of the Valkyries in Asgard, a title she gained on her wedding day. Her unhappy marriage to Odin resulted in her exile as well as being cut off from her family and native land, Vanaheim. She has lived alone in Midgard for a century, and she is called the Witch of the Woods.

Louis Cunningham, Ben Chapple, Evelyn Miller and Island Austin will play recurring roles of Modi, Magni, Gna and Thrud, respectively. Modi, Magni and Thrud are children of Thor and Sif, with Magni being the eldest son, Modi the middle child, and Thrud, their youngest. Gna is Odin’s Valkyrie commander.

What will Prime Video’s God of War show be about?

Based on the popular PlayStation video game, God of War  follows father and son, Kratos and 10-year-old Atreus, as they embark on a journey to spread the ashes of their late wife and mother, Faye. Through their adventures, Kratos tries to teach his son to be a better god, while Atreus tries to teach his father how to be a better human. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

Will there be multiple seasons of Prime Video’s God of War show?

Yes, the adaptation was officially greenlit in December 2022, and then, when Emmy-winning director E.O. Toye ( Shōgun , The Boys ) came aboard, the show received a two-season order.

Who else is behind Prime Video’s God of War TV show?

At first, Rafe Judkins, Hawk Ostby and Mark Fergus were attached to the project with Judkins in the showrunner role as well as an executive producer alongside Ostby and Fergus. The trio left the project in October 2024 after completing multiple scripts for the first season.

Ronald D. Moore came aboard as showrunner shortly after Deadline broke the news of creative changes. Toye, who will direct the first two episodes of the action-adventure series, joined the creative team Dec. 1, 2025. God of War i s co-produced by Sony Pictures Television and Amazon MGM Studios in association with PlayStation Productions and Moore’s Tall Ship Productions.

The video game was created by David Jaffe, who also created Twisted Metal which received a series adaptation on Peacock. Jaffe made some comments about the series' first-look image , released at the end of February 2026. This was before Bautista had taken over as Kratos, though.

articles.content:
Don Toliver is postponing a concert at London's 02 Arena after his Sunday night Manchester concert at Co-Op Live had to be evacuated after an unknown substance was released into the crowd.

"I Just Wanna Make Sure Everyone is Safe and the next Show goes on properly," Toliver wrote in an Instagram story on Monday. "My Heart and prayers are with with everyone that was injured last night at co-op live."

articles.summary: Image Courtesy of White Fox The voice behind Subaru Natsuki finally shared the anime's future even after Season 5. 2026 was a major year for Re:Zero -Starting Life in Another World– fans, as the anime not only aired its fourth season, but also commemorated its 10th anniversary. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The voice behind Subaru Natsuki finally shared the anime's future even after Season 5. 2026 was a major year for Re:Zero -Starting Life in Another World – fans, as the anime not only aired its fourth season, but also commemorated its 10th anniversary. The fifth season has already been confirmed, and it's going to be more intense than ever. The anime is based on an ongoing novel written by Tappei Nagatsuki and illustrated by Shinichirou Otsuka. As one of the biggest shows on Crunchyroll, it's no surprise Re:Zero was renewed for a fifth season not long after the fourth season finale.

The story is currently at a crucial phase as Subaru Natsuki was forced to witness his friends die in gruesome ways, forcing him to realize his weakness. Fans are more excited to see his journey continue in Season 5, especially after Rem woke up from her coma. During the anime's 10th anniversary event last week, the voice actors were in attendance and discussed their experiences working on the series for a decade. The anime has only just confirmed its fifth season, but Yusuke Kobayashi, the voice behind Natsuki Subaru, already revealed what to expect from the anime going forward.

Mantan Web shares his speech during the event, where Kobayashi says, “This toast is not a toast to a milestone, but the first call to continue running. We will continue to run for a long time to come, so we would be happy if you would continue to support and run with us in the world of Re:Zero , which may continue for decades to come.”

Since the novel is ongoing, it goes without saying that the fifth season won't be able to adapt the entire story. Since the anime is already popular, fans will keep getting sequel seasons until the story is over. Kobayashi's closing remarks during the event confirm that the anime has a long future ahead, which may even continue for decades. In February this year, Nagatsuki confirmed that the novel's story is only halfway over after 14 years of serialization. This means the anime will keep releasing more seasons for another decade or even more.

During the Season 5 announcement, Nagatsuki shared a special message to fans while dropping major hints about what to expect from the anime. While the creator didn't drop any major spoilers, he revealed that the but the journey from here on out will be even more grueling than ever, even comparing it to an inferno.

Season 4 was already a brutal journey , but Subaru won't be able to catch a break in the upcoming season as well. Nagatsuki also assures fans that the journey from here on out won't be all about hardship. Fans can also look forward to new encounters and exciting developments, which means we can expect new character introductions in Season 5 as well.

What are you most excited to see in the anime's Season 5? What do you hope will happen next in Subaru's journey? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

articles.content:
Sometimes all it takes is a little gusto and a cold pitch on LinkedIn to get a film rolling. At 23, Shlok Choudhari left college and followed his dream of filmmaking with his first short, 3:30 . Starring Priyanka Zemse, the black-and-white psychological noir follows a woman navigating Mumbai during the titular dark hour as medication, memory, and a growing sense of danger blur together. Choudhari drew on two real events he witnessed to explore trauma and misdiagnosis.

After screening at the Oscar-qualifying Tasveer Film Festival , the film is headed to the Yellowstone International Film Festival in Mumbai. Below, Choudhari and producer Sunil Sadarangani talk to Deadline about taking courage in filmmaking, developing themes around mental health awareness, and having an eye towards the future. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News 'Aurora' Short Film Team Angad Aulakh And Guy Kent On Tapping Into The Emotional Weight Of Self & Outer Space Documentary India's Yellowstone International Film Festival Announces Documentary And LGBTQIA+ Slates

DEADLINE: This is your first short film, and you’re 23. You should be in school, don’t you think? What compelled you to make this short?
